name: Uganda
summary: Half the world's mountain gorillas, the source of the Nile, the Rwenzori snowline on the equator and savanna parks within a day's drive of each other.

entries.caption: The Pearl of Africa
entries.description: Gorilla forest, the Mountains of the Moon and the Nile leaving Lake Victoria — all inside one small, green country.
entries.subject: mist over the forested hills of Bwindi Impenetrable National Park at sunrise

entries.caption: Green, End to End
entries.description: Crater lakes around Fort Portal, papyrus swamp on the Nile, and the Rwenzori snowline sitting on the equator.
entries.subject: the crater lakes and green hills around Fort Portal

entries.caption: Wildlife Encounters
entries.description: Mountain gorillas in Bwindi, chimpanzees in Kibale, and tree-climbing lions in the Ishasha sector.
entries.subject: a mountain gorilla in the Bwindi Impenetrable Forest

entries.caption: Queen Elizabeth and Kidepo
entries.description: Kob on the Kasenyi plains, elephant on the Kazinga Channel, and Kidepo Valley with almost nobody in it.
entries.subject: elephants on the Kazinga Channel in Queen Elizabeth National Park

entries.caption: The Mountains of the Moon
entries.description: The Rwenzori range holds glaciers three degrees from the equator, and Margherita Peak at 5,109 m.
entries.subject: the glaciated peaks of the Rwenzori Mountains above the moorland

entries.caption: Murchison, Through the Gap
entries.description: The entire Victoria Nile forced through a seven-metre gap and dropped forty-three metres into the gorge below.
entries.subject: the Nile forcing through the narrow gap at Murchison Falls

entries.caption: Where the Nile Begins
entries.description: The Nile leaves Lake Victoria at Jinja; Lake Bunyonyi holds twenty-nine islands and no bilharzia.
entries.subject: the islands and terraced shores of Lake Bunyonyi

entries.caption: The Ssese Islands
entries.description: Freshwater beaches and fishing villages on Lake Victoria, an hour and a half by ferry from Entebbe.
entries.subject: a sandy freshwater shore and fishing boats on the Ssese Islands

entries.caption: Kibale and Bwindi
entries.description: Thirteen primate species in Kibale, and in Bwindi a forest so old and so thick it was never logged.
entries.subject: dense canopy and buttressed trees in Kibale Forest

entries.caption: Grade Five on the Nile
entries.description: White-water rafting below the source at Jinja, plus bungee, kayaking and the long walk up Sipi.
entries.subject: white-water rafting on the Nile rapids at Jinja

entries.caption: The Kingdom of Buganda
entries.description: Uganda's kingdoms were never abolished for long — Buganda, Bunyoro and Toro still hold court.
entries.subject: a Buganda kingdom drummer in ceremonial bark cloth

entries.caption: Batwa and Karamojong
entries.description: The Batwa, forest people of the southwest, and the Karamojong cattle-keepers of the northeast plains.
entries.subject: a Karamojong herder with cattle on the plains of Karamoja

entries.caption: Rolex, Matoke, Luwombo
entries.description: Steamed green banana with groundnut sauce, chicken cooked in banana leaf, and an egg rolled in a chapati on every corner.
entries.subject: a street vendor cooking rolex chapati and eggs in Kampala

entries.caption: Imbalu and Nyege Nyege
entries.description: The Bagisu Imbalu season in the east, and four days of music on the banks of the Nile at Jinja.
entries.subject: drummers and dancers at the Imbalu ceremony in eastern Uganda

entries.caption: Bark Cloth and Basketry
entries.description: Bark cloth from the mutuba fig, made in Buganda for six hundred years and now UNESCO-listed.
entries.subject: a craftsman beating bark cloth from a mutuba fig tree

entries.caption: The Kasubi Tombs
entries.description: The burial ground of four Buganda kings, thatched, enormous and rebuilt by the clans who have always maintained it.
entries.subject: the great thatched dome of the Kasubi Tombs in Kampala

entries.caption: Kingdoms Still Standing
entries.description: Royal drums, regalia and clan structures that survived the protectorate, the 1966 crisis and the 1970s.
entries.subject: royal regalia and drums inside a Buganda kingdom palace

entries.caption: Kampala on Seven Hills
entries.description: A capital built across hills and traffic, with the Gaddafi Mosque minaret giving the best view of all of it.
entries.subject: the hills and rooftops of Kampala seen from the Gaddafi Mosque minaret

entries.caption: Minaret, Dome and Thatch
entries.description: The Uganda National Mosque, the Namirembe and Rubaga cathedrals facing each other across two hills.
entries.subject: the minaret of the Uganda National Mosque above Kampala

entries.caption: Boda Bodas and Owino
entries.description: The boda boda is the transport system; Owino market is where the whole city goes to buy everything.
entries.subject: boda boda motorcycle taxis waiting at a busy Kampala street stage

entries.caption: Villages at the Forest Edge
entries.description: Community walks in Buhoma and Nkuringo, run by the villages that share the forest with the gorillas.
entries.subject: a community village walk beside the forest edge at Buhoma

entries.caption: Sipi, Elgon, Bisoke
entries.description: Three waterfalls and a coffee walk at Sipi, then the long crater rim of Mount Elgon above it.
entries.subject: the Sipi Falls dropping off the Mount Elgon escarpment

entries.caption: Lodges at the Forest Edge
entries.description: Small lodges on the Bwindi ridge and the Kazinga Channel, close enough to walk to the trailhead after breakfast.
entries.subject: a lodge terrace overlooking the Bwindi forest ridge at dawn

entries.caption: The Gorilla Permit
entries.description: Permit revenue funds the park and pays a share to the parishes around it — which is why the gorilla numbers are rising.
entries.subject: rangers and trackers setting out on a gorilla trek in Bwindi

entries.caption: Crater Lakes at First Light
entries.description: The Ndali-Kasenda crater field before the haze lifts, and the Ishasha fig trees in the late afternoon.
entries.subject: morning mist on the Ndali-Kasenda crater lakes near Fort Portal

entries.caption: Kidepo Valley
entries.description: The furthest park from Kampala and the emptiest: Narus valley, the Morungole range, and cheetah nobody photographs.
entries.subject: the Narus valley and mountains of Kidepo Valley National Park

entries.caption: Half the World's Gorillas
entries.description: Nowhere else puts gorillas, chimpanzees, the Big Five, a snowline and the Nile within one week of driving.
entries.subject: a silverback mountain gorilla resting in the Bwindi undergrowth
